 WNBA WNBA championship may be decided on a Thursday morning because an NBA game took priority
 The league, facing a logistics nightmare for Game 6 between the Golden State Valkyries and the Atlanta Dream, opted to play the key contest with a 12:30 p.m. ET/9:30 a.m. PT tipoff. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Isobel Borlase of the Atlanta Dream, right, shoots against Veronica Burton of the Golden State Valkyries during Game 4 of the WNBA Finals at State Farm Arena in Atlanta. Kevin C. Cox / Getty Share Add NBC News to Google Oct. 26, 2026, 4:38 PM EDT  /  Updated   Oct. 26, 2026, 6:39 PM EDT By David K. Li The WNBA scheduled its potential championship-clinching game for 12:30 p.m. ET Thursday, the league announced , settling a logistical nightmare that appeared to have few satisfactory solutions.
 The Golden State Valkyries and the Atlanta Dream’s Game 6 had always been set for Thursday night in Georgia with its location and exact tipoff time listed as TBD because of a series of scheduling conflicts.
 The Dream’s playoff home, State Farm Arena, has an Atlanta Hawks game scheduled for Thursday night.
 “We thank the NBA, Dream, Valkyries, Hawks, State Farm Arena and USA Network for the collaboration and flexibility that made this move possible,” retiring WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert said in a statement Monday afternoon. 
 The Dream played most of its 2026 season at the 3,500-seat Gateway Center Arena at College Park, the league’s smallest building. The team had been able to move major regular-season games and all playoff contests to State Farm Arena, the 17,000-seat home of the NBA’s Atlanta Hawks.
 But with Game 6 set for Thursday, the same day as a 7 p.m. Hawks game against the Cleveland Cavaliers at State Farm, that big venue was not available for a primetime women’s game.
 If the Valkyries win Monday’s Game 5 in San Francisco, their West Coast fans would have to get to a TV by 9:30 a.m. PT Thursday and possibly pop champagne bottles before noon should Golden State wrap it up in Atlanta.

 Slide 1 of 1 “The sellout crowds and extraordinary atmosphere of State Farm Arena for Games 3 and 4 were a tremendous success and we’re excited to give thousands more fans the opportunity to experience Game 6 with a championship on the line,” she said.
 The WNBA, the arena, the broadcasters and the teams had to make adjustments just to get Games 3 and 4 into State Farm.
 Game 3 was moved up by one day to Wednesday , rescheduled from Thursday, when State Farm played host to a Sombr concert.
 Game 4 was shifted to an earlier time Saturday, to 1 p.m. from 3:30 p.m. ET, so arena workers had enough time to convert State Farm for the Hawks’ game against the Houston Rockets that night .
